terms.comment: With an object, an infinitive or ut. With a dative, to wish someone something (tibi bona optāvī omnia, Plaut. Rud. 3.2.25), though more often something bad (Lewis & Short). Optā! is “make a wish!”.
With the present subjunctive for a wish that may come true (utinam veniat!), with the imperfect for one that is not true now (utinam adesset!, I wish he were here).

terms.gloss: I wish (that) …, of what is not so
terms.comment: The idiom of Cicero’s letters, with a subjunctive or an accusative.

terms.gloss: wish greatly; wish someone (a happy birthday)
evidence: Traupman 409: Novum Annum laetum tibi exoptō
Cic. Off. 3.94: Thēseō cum trēs optātiōnēs Neptūnus dedisset (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: atque utinam continuō ad complexum meae Tulliae, ad ōsculum Atticae possim currere!
phrases.english: if only I could run straight to a hug from my Tullia and a kiss from Attica!

phrases.latin: spūmantemque darī pecora inter inertia vōtīs optat aprum, aut fulvum dēscendere monte leōnem
phrases.english: and among the tame flocks he wishes a foaming boar might be granted to his prayers, or a tawny lion come down from the mountain
